facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms
A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, indicating acute coronary syndrome.

The patient developed akinesia of all apical segments, later extending to mid-segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35%, leading to suspicion of takotsubo syndrome.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, indicating ventricular tachycardia.
The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, indicating myocardial infarction.
It explains the uncovered finding of significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis and subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch.

rationales.F02: Multiple risk factors increase the likelihood of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F03: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions suggest a history of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F08: Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis is a strong indicator of coronary artery disease and increases the risk of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction, but less typical for takotsubo syndrome.
rationales.F10: Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch is a strong indicator of coronary artery disease and increases the risk of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F11: Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation are strong indicators of ventricular tachycardia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with ST-segment elevation, recurrent ventricular tachycardia, and new QTc prolongation, along with the echocardiographic findings of akinesia of all apical segments and severely reduced LVEF, are more consistent with Takotsubo Syndrome, despite the presence of coronary artery disease and prior myocardial infarctions.
